card.name: Commas and joins in step-by-step instructions
card.fires_on: Commas, 'and', 'by' or a noun right after an instruction clause, where the sentence is about to add a further step or condition. Seen in recipes, technical how-to text and usage directions.

modes.label: Comma between steps
modes.description: A comma ends an instruction clause and the next action follows.
modes.example: Pare a pound of potatoes, slice them thin<<,>> peel about a pound of large onions,

modes.label: Noun in a spec or format rule
modes.description: A noun such as name or number is followed by a detail on how it is written or placed.

modes.label: Joiner after an instruction
modes.description: A joiner such as 'and' or 'by' follows an instruction and adds the means or the result.
modes.example: warm IMCIVREE prior to administration<< by>> rolling the vial gently between the palms

card.writes: It seems to suppress words like 'preceded' or 'surrounded', so the text continues with a new step instead of a described relation.
card.plain: It fires at the point in a set of directions where one step ends and the next step or detail is about to start.
